name: Strasbourg Airport
before:
Strasbourg's airport, at Entzheim 10 km west south west of the city. It handled 1,308,984 passengers in 2025 from a single two storey terminal, with check in and arrivals downstairs and the departure lounges and four air bridge gates above.

The train is the thing to use. Entzheim-Aéroport station sits at the airport on the Strasbourg to Molsheim line, and TER Grand Est trains reach Strasbourg-Ville in seven to twelve minutes. There is no direct bus or tram into the city, so the train really is the answer.

High speed rail also explains the airport's shape. The LGV Est cut the journey from Paris so sharply, to one hour forty eight minutes after the second phase opened in July 2016, that Air France gave up flying the route in 2013 and puts passengers on the train instead. Traffic has nonetheless grown since 2011.

The nearest larger airports are Basel Mulhouse, 154 km south, and Stuttgart, 168 km north east.
after:
Strasbourg's airport, at Entzheim 10 km west south west of the city. It handled about 1.3 million passengers in 2025 from a single terminal.

The train is the thing to use. Entzheim-Aéroport station sits at the airport, and its TER Grand Est trains reach Strasbourg station in eight minutes, the airport says.

High speed rail also explains the airport's shape. Flights to Paris Charles de Gaulle stopped in 2013, and Eurostat's figures show the last to Orly in 2016. Traffic has nonetheless grown since 2011.

The nearest bigger airport is Karlsruhe/Baden-Baden in Germany, about 42 km north east in a straight line. Basel Mulhouse is about 105 km south and Stuttgart about 118 km east, and both are larger again.

claims.note: Replaces 'The nearest larger airports are Basel Mulhouse ... and Stuttgart'. Karlsruhe/Baden-Baden is nearer than either and handled 2,257,542 passengers in 2025 (ADV; Eurostat 2,256,875) against Strasbourg's 1.3 million. It is the nearest airport with scheduled flights: Lahr (23.9 km), Phalsbourg (40.4 km) and Colmar (51.6 km) have none. Straight line 42.7 km on OurAirports' coordinates and 42.1 km on Wikipedia's, both at 51 degrees.

opinion.text: The train is the thing to use.
opinion.why: The old text's advice, kept: the station is at the terminal and the airport runs up to five shuttle trains an hour (sourced, held back).

opinion.text: High speed rail also explains the airport's shape.
opinion.why: The old text's framing, kept. Wikipedia ties the fall in flying to the first phase of the LGV Est, and Eurostat's Paris routes fall from 1,006,961 passengers in 2006 to 438,181 in 2008 before stopping.
